rfm_tuples.R: ADMA Biologics Issues Statement Refuting Unsubstantiated, Misleading and Inaccurate Allegations by Culper Research... Demand for ASCENIV is real and growing... Distributors must maintain a level of safety stock... an average of 84 and 48 days on hand, respectively, for ASCENIV [in excess of distributors' minimum requirements as of Jan 5 and Mar 22] (2026-03-27 8-K/PR)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A: Cross-check ADMA's own disclosed inventory days vs typical CSO/CIVO benchmarks; Mode-B: re-check claim against Q1 actual revenue print and BIVIGAM trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (issuer's own disclosed inventory days) + SEC 10-Q 0001140361-26-019336 + 8-K 0001140361-26-019295
rfm_tuples.M_value: ADMA's own data shows 84 days of ASCENIV inventory ABOVE safety stock at Jan 5 2026 falling to 48 days by Mar 22 2026 — a 36-day inventory drawdown in 11 weeks. Total inventory days: 128 -> 90 for ASCENIV; 129 -> 92 for BIVIGAM. These are extraordinarily high for any drug class. The Q1 outcome (BIVIGAM revenue -54% YoY, FY26 guidance cut) is exactly what one would expect if distributors had been ahead on inventory and were now destocking. ADMA's own May 6 PR confirmed an Audit Committee internal review was opened in response to the allegations.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: ADMA's refutation cited its own data which actually corroborates rather than rebuts the channel-stuffing narrative: distributor days of coverage materially higher than a typical 30-60-day specialty pharma channel, declining sharply through Q1. The subsequent revenue collapse and the activation of an internal forensic audit (acknowledged in 5/6 PR) confirm the short thesis had material substance. Issuer's framing as 'temporary market dislocation' shifts blame to industry pricing while the timing pattern (stuffing pre-Jan-12-guide, destocking through Q1) fits the channel-fill thesis.

The disclosure satisfies Mode-A (the fact is stated), but Mode-B reveals that this structure means a small group of distributors can essentially set ADMA's quarterly revenue, and the destocking dynamic seen in Q1 demonstrates the asymmetric tail risk.

summary: ADMA presents a near-prototype Signal OS R/f/M short profile: aggressive bullish multi-year guidance issued Jan 12 2026 (with FY29 target of $1.1B revenue / $700M EBITDA) was retracted 114 days later, with FY26 revenue cut 12-16% and FY26 EBITDA cut 17-26%, plus long-term guidance withdrawn entirely. Channel-stuffing allegations from Culper Research (Mar 24) were rebutted using ADMA's own data showing 84-128 days of distributor inventory — figures that corroborate rather than refute the thesis, particularly given the realized Q1 BIVIGAM revenue collapse (-54% YoY). Form 4 evidence is decisively negative: zero C-suite open-market purchases despite -62% drawdown; CEO sold $4.5M via 10b5-1 plan adopted Nov 14 2025 with first sale dated to the 10-K filing day; Director Elms sold $8.8M in June 2025; only ~$418k in tiny director purchases (Jerrold Grossman family-stewardship and Elms pre-short-report). Customer concentration (71% Q1 revenue from 2 distributors, 82% A/R) makes channel mechanics decisive. Audit Committee 'completed' a forensic review in 6 weeks and disclosed via earnings PR rather than standalone filing. Verdict: SHORT-tier despite the offsetting positive FDA approval — the disclosure-trust deficit is too large.
